content.value_statement: Vector search systems often trade recall, latency, and memory without clear tuning guidance. This skill provides parameter templates, quantization choices, and monitoring patterns for production indexes.
actual_capabilities: Recommends HNSW parameters for dataset size, recall goals, latency targets, and memory limits.
Provides benchmark templates for measuring recall, build time, search latency, and memory use.
Explains scalar, product, binary, FP16, and FP32 quantization tradeoffs.
Shows Qdrant collection settings for recall, speed, balanced, and memory-focused profiles.
Includes monitoring patterns for latency percentiles, recall, throughput, and build performance.
limitations: Does not benchmark a live vector database without user-provided data and execution steps.
Recommendations must be validated against real queries, embeddings, and production traffic patterns.
Examples focus on HNSW, quantization, Qdrant, and general ANN tuning concepts.
Does not replace vendor documentation for version-specific database behavior.

use_cases.title: Tune Production Recall
use_cases.description: Balance efSearch, M, and quantization choices against a target recall and latency budget.

use_cases.title: Plan Vector Memory Capacity
use_cases.description: Estimate storage needs for embedding dimensions, vector count, index overhead, and compression strategy.

use_cases.title: Compare Database Settings
use_cases.description: Create Qdrant collection profiles for speed, recall, balanced performance, or reduced memory use.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Index Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new vector search service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a vector index type for my dataset. I have [vector count], [dimensions], [target recall], [latency target], and [memory budget].

prompt_templates.title: Tune HNSW Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer improving an existing HNSW index.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest HNSW M, efConstruction, and efSearch values for [vector count], [recall target], [update rate], and [maximum query latency].

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Quantization
prompt_templates.scenario: Team reducing memory use without losing too much recall.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare FP32, FP16, INT8 scalar, product quantization, and binary quantization for [dimensions], [vector count], and [recall tolerance].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Benchmark Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production validation before changing index settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a benchmark plan for our vector search index using real queries, ground truth results, latency percentiles, recall metrics, and memory measurements.

output_examples.input: Recommend HNSW settings for two million vectors with 768 dimensions, 95 percent recall, and 20 ms latency.
output_examples.output: Start with M around 48, efConstruction near 256, and efSearch near 128. Benchmark efSearch values from 64 to 256 against real queries before rollout.

output_examples.input: How can we reduce memory for a large semantic search index?
output_examples.output: Evaluate INT8 scalar quantization first, then product quantization if memory remains too high. Measure recall loss, rescoring quality, and p95 latency.

output_examples.input: What should we monitor after changing index parameters?
output_examples.output: Track recall against ground truth, p50, p95, and p99 latency, query throughput, build time, index size, and drift in representative queries.

best_practices: Benchmark with production-like queries and known ground truth before changing index settings.
Tune one major parameter at a time so recall and latency changes are attributable.
Monitor recall, latency percentiles, throughput, memory, and rebuild cost after deployment.
anti_patterns: Optimizing for low latency without measuring recall loss.
Choosing aggressive quantization before testing representative embeddings and queries.
Ignoring index build time, warmup, and maintenance windows for large collections.

faq.question: What vector index sizes does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers small flat indexes, HNSW for medium and large datasets, and quantized approaches for larger deployments.

faq.question: Can it tune Qdrant collections?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Qdrant examples for HNSW, quantization, optimizer settings, and search parameters.

faq.question: Does it run benchmarks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides benchmark templates and measurement guidance that users can adapt to their own environment.

faq.question: How should I choose efSearch?
faq.answer: Start from the recall target, test several values, and select the lowest value that meets recall and latency goals.

faq.question: When should I use quantization?
faq.answer: Use quantization when memory, storage, or cache pressure limits performance, then validate recall impact with real queries.

faq.question: Is this skill limited to one database?
faq.answer: No. Qdrant examples are included, but the HNSW, quantization, and monitoring guidance applies broadly.
